newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs rally, end up sharply on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs rally, end up sharply on weather concerns.

text.p: CME hog futures rallied from mixed values early as weather concerns grew and prompted buying that pushed prices up into buy stops. Early sharp losses were pared in pork bellies on spillover demand and short covering, traders said.

Hogs closed 1.275 cent a lb higher to 0.225 lower with December pacing the advance at 58.900 cents and February ending up 0.700 at 76.100 cents. Pork bellies closed 0.925 to 0.500 lower with February off 0.675 at 78.525 cents.
Concern that a storm will roll out of the southwest into the Midwest early next week prompted much of the rally, traders said.
"It's (storm) going to move up from Texas all the way into the upper Midwest," said Dave Maher, livestock analyst for Securities Corp of Iowa.

Maher cited local weather forecasts for six to nine inches of snow by Wednesday in Iowa. He and other traders and analysts noted that pork fundamentals may have found a bottom, based on the action in pork prices Thursday and early Friday.
Pork cutout values were mostly unchanged Thursday after falling more than $5 from the first of the month and cash pork prices were mixed at noon Friday.
Rand Financials and Rosenthal Collins bought December and bought back early short sales in February. Refco also purchased February with buy stops touched off in both months, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought February 74 calls and LIT division of First Options sold 76 calls early. Locals bought calls and sold puts on the belly, pit sources added.
After tumbling as much as 2.700 cents in February early, pork belly futures rallied on local short covering and mixed commission house demand following the rally in hog futures, traders said.

Bellies fell early when local profit taking met little buying interest. Fund sell stops took prices down sharply with locals also turning to the sell side on the break. Futures then worked back up after light commercial support developed. Fundamentals remain strong in pork bellies, they said.

Belly movement into storage will remain light as the premium of futures to cash is too small to encourage storings. Demand for bacon has also been much better than expected for this time of year, sources added.
